product: The Complete System for Mature Women's Skin ($121.07)
avatar_brief: Woman 50-58, at a kitchen table with a phone propped against a fruit bowl, scrolling on a second phone. Morning light. Delivery is sceptical-turning-curious — she is reading other people's words aloud, not making claims of her own.
hook: Thirty-four thousand people reviewed this before I did. I read the one-stars first.
first_frame: Her holding a phone showing a wall of review text, screen angled to camera so the volume of it reads even if the words don't.

beats.vo: Thirty-four thousand people reviewed this before I did. I read the one-stars first.
beats.visual: Phone held up, review list scrolling, kitchen behind.

beats.vo: That's my rule. If the complaints are all about shipping and none about the product, that tells you something.
beats.visual: She scrolls with her thumb, genuinely reading, not performing.

beats.vo: Eight hundred and twenty-three thousand customers. At that size you can't hide a bad product behind good marketing.
beats.visual: Puts the phone down, picks up the Frøya system box.

beats.vo: Four steps, arctic plants, dermatologist-tested. It supports the skin barrier in 7 days.
beats.visual: The four jars come out of the box onto the table, one at a time.

beats.vo: A hundred and twenty-one dollars with sixty days to change your mind. I let other people take that risk first.
beats.visual: Back to her face, morning light, no makeup.

beats.vo: The Complete System for Mature Women's Skin. Frøya. Go read the one-stars yourself.
beats.visual: Four jars on the table, phone beside them. Brand name on screen.

hook: I don't trust brands. I trust the number of strangers who bothered to come back and write something.
first_frame: Laptop on her knees on a stairwell, review page on screen, her face lit by it from below.

beats.vo: I don't trust brands. I trust the number of strangers who bothered to come back and write something.
beats.visual: Laptop on knees, review page, screen light on her face.

beats.vo: Writing a review is annoying. People only do it when something genuinely worked or genuinely didn't.
beats.visual: She scrolls, pauses on a longer review, keeps scrolling.

beats.vo: This one has thirty-four thousand of them, and it's the day balm that keeps coming up.
beats.visual: Cut to the day balm jar sitting on the step beside her.

beats.vo: Sea buckthorn and pomegranate. Studies show 22% younger skin, 95% reported youthful glow.
beats.visual: She opens it one-handed, presses some into the back of her hand.

beats.vo: Under thirty dollars, which is the price where I'll take a stranger's word for it.
Anti-Age and Insane Glow Day Balm, from Frøya. Let the reviews do the work.
